newsitem.title: UK: NWE fuel oil barges close steady, cargoes talk low.
newsitem.headline: NWE fuel oil barges close steady, cargoes talk low.

text.p: European high sulphur fuel oil barges closed steady on Friday but at the high side of the week's range while cargoes talked a little weaker with supplies of Russian said to be available on the market, traders said.

High sulphur barges traded late on Friday at $85.50 and $85.25 -- or within Thursday's closing range -- after earlier deals at $84 and $83.50. Late offers were reported in the $85.75/$86 range but no deals were heard.
"The sellers are running away so buying suddenly set in," one trader said, commenting on the market's rise in the afternoon.

Some traders said the lower levels earlier in the day were set by some players interested in seeing lower cargo quotes for pricing, while others said that buying interest was dulled by crude's fall last night.
Bunkers were a little weaker to steady, with 380 CST fuel done at $85.50 and $86.50 and 180 CST traded at $91.
Low sulphur barges were very quiet, with some sellers holding at the $97 mark while others cut their asking price 50 cents to $1, but no buying interest was seen at those levels.
"I think people may be waiting for prices to drop further with crude," one Rotterdam-based trader said.
High sulphur cargoes were offered a little lower, with one trader saying that he cut his price for Russian M-100 cracked to two means flat but buying interest was $1.50 to $2 lower.
"There are supplies there, we have a cargo every three days," the seller said, adding he sold an M-100 cracked cargo on Thursday to a Mediterranean buyer at $81 cif, $1 below deals he had last week.
But other traders said high sulphur would continue to draw strength from the fact that the Russian supplies were being absorbed by the market.
One percent was also said to be weaker in line with weaker swaps and low buying interest. There was unconfirmed talk of a cargo changing hands on Friday at $98 cif or around the $88/$89 fob level.

A buyer who was actively seeking a cargo earlier this week said he withdrew from the market and will be moving two cargoes he picked up earlier to Israel and the Far East. Only one other buyer was heard on the market.
